core: Abstraction manages complexity by exposing only the essential features of something through a simpler interface while hiding the implementation details.
Information hiding: separating what a component does (its interface/specification) from how it does it (its implementation), so the hidden details can change without disturbing users.
Levels/layers of abstraction: hardware -> operating system -> application, each layer presenting an interface to the layer above and hiding the layer below; abstraction barriers isolate the levels.

Concrete examples: driving a car through pedals/wheel without engine internals; calling a function by its signature without its body; an API; data abstraction / abstract data types where the operations that exist are separated from how they are implemented.
An abstract data type (ADT) specifies a set of values and operations independently of any particular implementation.
supporting: Abstraction is one of the four pillars of computational thinking (with decomposition, pattern recognition, and algorithmic thinking).
Abstraction is also one of the four pillars of object-oriented programming (named, not owned, here).
The term information hiding originates with David Parnas's 1972 paper.

claims.claim: Abstraction focuses on the essential information about something while ignoring or hiding irrelevant implementation details, exposing behavior through a simpler interface.
Information hiding separates what a component does (its specification/interface) from how it does it (its implementation body); the concept was introduced by David Parnas in a 1972 CACM paper.

In a layered system, horizontal abstraction barriers isolate different levels; procedures at each level are the interfaces that connect levels, so a change to a lower-level implementation does not force changes in higher-level code that uses only the interface.
An abstract data type is a set of data values and associated operations that are precisely specified independently of any particular implementation.
Data abstraction lets a program isolate how a compound data object is used from the details of how it is constructed, using selector and constructor procedures as the interface.

Abstraction is one of the pillars of computational thinking; Wing characterizes computational thinking as using abstraction and decomposition when attacking a large complex task or designing a large complex system.
Abstraction (hide detail behind an interface; what-not-how) is a distinct technique from decomposition (split a problem into smaller parts); computational thinking uses both together.
